title: Halmos counterexample: pendingPhUSD() view-helper underflows on realistic inputs
property: For every (amount, phUSDDebt, accPhUSDPerShareInit, phUSDPerSecond, timeElapsed, totalStaked) in stated bounds, pendingPhUSD() must not revert.
counterexample_summary: Halmos found multiple witnesses where the final return `(amount * _accPhUSDPerShare) / PRECISION - phUSDDebt` underflows. Witnesses include large `phUSDDebt` (anchored from an earlier state) combined with small projected accumulator growth.
interpretation: Confirms CODE-007 view-DoS reachability with a mathematical proof. Front-ends and integrators that call `pendingPhUSD(user)` will revert with Panic 0x11 for any user whose `phUSDDebt` exceeds the projected `(amount * _accPhUSDPerShare) / PRECISION`. Most commonly produced by the post-pauseWithdraw staleness pattern of CODE-002, but also by other state-debt drift scenarios.

crossReference.CODE-007: Verifies the view-revert claim. The view's projected-acc arithmetic does NOT widen the safe region — projected acc is bounded below by the stored acc, so the projection only helps when `phUSDPerSecond > 0` and `timeElapsed > 0`. The underflow path remains reachable.

remediation: Clamp the final subtraction in both view helpers: `return lhs >= debt ? lhs - debt : 0;`.
